Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement  
Member: Skyler Ellison  
Member ID: W656322877  
Plan: Premera Blue Cross Commercial/ACA  
Requested procedure: Total shoulder arthroplasty, CPT 23472  
Reference number: POC-8E86334152-82903  
Denial date: August 9, 2026

Dear Member Appeals Department:

I am appealing Premera’s denial of authorization for total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472. The denial states that the submitted imaging findings do not support medical necessity. The clinical records directly address the imaging requirement and the other medical-necessity factors in Premera’s publicly posted MEDICAL POLICY – 7.01.590 Shoulder Arthroplasty, effective April 1, 2026, last revised March 23, 2026.

The policy states:

“Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following:

Irregular joint surfaces

Glenoid sclerosis

Glenoid osteophyte changes

Flattened glenoid

Cystic changes in the humeral head

Joint space narrowing”

The May 27, 2026 shoulder radiographs show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. These findings satisfy multiple imaging findings listed in the policy, including joint-space narrowing, glenoid osteophyte changes, glenoid sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. The CT also confirms an intact rotator cuff. Therefore, the submitted imaging does support destructive degenerative disease of the shoulder under the policy criteria.

The other documented clinical requirements are also supported:

- Symptoms have progressed for 14 months, with pain unrelieved by rest.
- The condition causes substantial functional impairment. I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.
- Examination shows glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees.
- I used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 22, 2026 provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- I completed 10 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy from May 5 through July 14, 2026, focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening. This exceeds the policy’s stated six-week physical-measures trial.
- The CT confirms an intact rotator cuff, and cuff strength is intact, supporting the proposed total shoulder procedure rather than a procedure selected for an irreparable cuff tear.
- The records document no active infection. I am also a nonsmoker, have a BMI of 29, and have no untreated substance-use condition identified in the submitted summary.

Premera’s policy states:

“Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following:

Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration

Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration”

The 14-month history of progressive pain and the documented inability to reach overhead, dress independently, and sleep on the affected side satisfy these requirements.

The policy also states:

“Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following:

Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics

Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate”

The six months of unsuccessful NSAID treatment and the corticosteroid injection with only temporary partial relief document failed conservative medication management. The physical therapy discharge note documents 10 weeks of supervised therapy and 20 completed visits.

Please overturn the denial and approve the requested total shoulder arthroplasty, CPT 23472.

If Premera maintains the denial, please provide, at no cost, the specific medical-necessity criterion that Premera believes was not met, the complete clinical review criteria or guideline applied, the medical-review rationale, and all documents and records relied upon in making the determination. Please also identify whether the denial was based on a policy other than MEDICAL POLICY – 7.01.590 Shoulder Arthroplasty.

Please treat this letter as a request for internal review and include the following with the appeal:

- The May 27, 2026 shoulder radiographs and CT report;
- The physical therapy discharge note documenting treatment from May 5 through July 14, 2026;
- Medication and injection treatment history;
- The orthopedic examination findings; and
- The surgeon’s supporting clinical statement from Reyes, MD.

Please send the appeal determination in writing. Thank you for your prompt review.

Sincerely,

Skyler Ellison
